proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(A=USV^{\top}\).  The span assumptions give unique coordinates \(x,y\in\mathbb R^r\) such that \(u=x^{\top}V^{\top}\) and \(v=Uy\), with \(\|x\|_2=\|u\|_2\) and \(\|y\|_2=\|v\|_2\).  Conditional on \(X\), the matrices \(\widehat U,\widehat S,\widehat V\) are fixed.  By the block independence in \(\textnormal{ass:gaussian-blocks}\),
\[
 (e\widehat V)^{\top}/\sigma\sim N(0,I_r),\qquad
 \widehat U^{\top}f/\sigma\sim N(0,I_r),
\]
independently of one another and of \(X\).  This proves the asserted conditional experiment \(Z=m+\xi\), \(\xi\sim N(0,I_{2r})\).  Moreover,
\[
 \sigma^2m_p^{\top}Dm_q
 =u\widehat V\widehat S^{-1}\widehat U^{\top}v
 =uX_r^+v=\theta_X.
\]

We next prove the donor comparison, including the constants needed by the stated allowance.  Put \(e_0=\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), \(L=U^{\top}\widehat U\), \(M=V^{\top}\widehat V\), and suppose first that \(e_0\le cn/4\).  The singular equations and the fact that \((I-UU^{\top})A=0\) give
\[
 \|(I-UU^{\top})\widehat U\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le {e_0\over cn-e_0}=:\lambda,
 \qquad
 \|(I-VV^{\top})\widehat V\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lambda.
\]
Indeed, the left sides multiplied by \(\widehat S\) are respectively \((I-UU^{\top})E\widehat V\) and \((I-VV^{\top})E^{\top}\widehat U\), while the least retained singular value is at least \(cn-e_0\) by the min--max formula.  Hence \(\lambda\le1/3\),
\[
 s_r(L),s_r(M)\ge\sqrt{1-\lambda^2},qquad
 \|LL^{\top}-I_r\|_{\mathrm{op}},\|MM^{\top}-I_r\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lambda^2.
\]
Let \(F=X-X_r\).  Orthogonality of the truncated singular expansion gives
\[
 F=(I-\widehat U\widehat U^{\top})F(I-\widehat V\widehat V^{\top}),
 \qquad \|F\|_{\mathrm{op}}=s_{r+1}(X)\le e_0.
\]
Consequently, for \(B_X=U^{\top}X_rV=L\widehat S M^{\top}\) and \(\gamma=\|U^{\top}EV\|_{\mathrm{op}}\),
\[
 \|B_X-S\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\gamma+\lambda^2e_0,
 \qquad \|B_X^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le {3\over2cn}.
\]
Direct multiplication gives the basis-invariant sandwich identity
\[
 T_X:=V^{\top}X_r^+U=(MM^{\top})B_X^{-1}(LL^{\top}).
\]
Expanding its three factors around \(S^{-1}\), and using
\(B_X^{-1}-S^{-1}=B_X^{-1}(S-B_X)S^{-1}\), yields
\[
 \|T_X-S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le {3\lambda^2\over cn}+{3(\gamma+\lambda^2e_0)\over2c^2n^2}
 \le {3\gamma\over2c^2n^2}+{6e_0^2\over c^3n^3}.
\]
For the last inequality, use \(\lambda^2\le16e_0^2/(9c^2n^2)\) and \(e_0\le cn/4\).  It follows that
\[
 |\theta_X-\theta|
 =|x^{\top}(T_X-S^{-1})y|
 \le\|u\|_2\|v\|_2
 \left\{{3\gamma\over2c^2n^2}+{6e_0^2\over c^3n^3}\right\}.
\]

For completeness, the Gaussian bounds used below follow directly from exponential moments.  If \(g\sim N(0,I_d)\), optimizing the moment-generating function of \(\|g\|_2^2\) gives
\[
 \Pr\{\|g\|_2>\sqrt d+\sqrt{2x}\}\le e^{-x}.
\]
For an \(n\)-by-\(n\) standard Gaussian matrix \(G_0\), Gaussian interpolation applied to \(y^{\top}G_0x\), with comparison process \(g^{\top}y+h^{\top}x\), gives \(\mathbb E\|G_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt n\): its increment comparison is
\[
 \|y-y'\|_2^2+\|x-x'\|_2^2-
 \mathbb E[(y^{\top}G_0x-y'^{\top}G_0x')^2]
 =2(1-\langle x,x'\rangle)(1-\langle y,y'\rangle)\ge0.
\]
The interpolation identity is obtained first for finite nets by differentiating the log-sum-exp and then by monotone net approximation.  For the concentration step, let \(F\) be any smooth one-Lipschitz function of a standard Gaussian vector and put \(\Lambda(t)=\log\mathbb E e^{tF}\).  Differentiating entropy along the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck interpolation and using Gaussian integration by parts gives
\[
 \operatorname{Ent}(e^{tF})\le {t^2\over2}\mathbb E e^{tF}.
\]
Indeed, the derivative of entropy along the interpolation is the negative expected squared gradient divided by the interpolated density, and the gradient contraction contributes \(e^{-2s}\); its integral over \(s\ge0\) is \(1/2\).  Dividing by \(\mathbb E e^{tF}\) gives \(t\Lambda'(t)-\Lambda(t)\le t^2/2\), and integration from zero to \(t\) gives
\(\mathbb E\exp\{t(F-\mathbb EF)\}\le e^{t^2/2}\).  Approximation extends this result to \(F(G_0)=\|G_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Chernoff optimization therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}>3\sigma\sqrt n\}\le e^{-n/2}.
\]

Let \(H_n\) be the intersection of the four events
\[
 \|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\sigma\sqrt n,\quad
 \|U^{\top}EV\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\sigma(r+\sqrt{12\ell_n}),\quad
 \|\xi_p\|_2,\|\xi_q\|_2\le\sqrt r+\sqrt{12\ell_n}.
\]
The entries of \(U^{\top}EV/\sigma\) are independent standard normals, so its operator norm is bounded by its Frobenius norm.  Applying the displayed vector bound with \(x=6\ell_n\) to that \(r^2\)-vector and to each projected-noise \(r\)-vector, and using \(r\le r_0\), gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(H_n^c)
 \le e^{-n/2}+3e^{-6\ell_n}
 =e^{-n/2}+3(e+n)^{-6}.
\]
For \(n\ge144\sigma^2/c^2\), \(H_n\) implies \(e_0\le cn/4\).  It also implies \(G_n\), by the min--max perturbation inequalities
\(s_r(X)\ge s_r(A)-e_0\) and \(s_1(X)\le s_1(A)+e_0\), together with \(c\le1\) and \(C_0\ge2\).  On \(H_n\), the preceding sandwich bound and \(\ell_n\ge1\) imply
\[
 \|T_X-S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_T{\ell_n\over n^2}.
\]
Moreover \(s_r(M)\ge\sqrt8/3\), and therefore
\[
 \|u\|_2\le {3\sigma A_\xi\over\sqrt8}
 (\|Z_p\|_2+\sqrt{\ell_n}),qquad
 \|v\|_2\le {3\sigma A_\xi\over\sqrt8}
 (\|Z_q\|_2+\sqrt{\ell_n}).
\]
Substitution proves \(|\theta_X-\theta|\le d_n\) on \(H_n\), because \(K_0=9A_\xi^2C_T/8\).  This proves the asserted probability bound.

It remains to verify the expectation statement.  Write \(U_0=\|u\|_2\), \(V_0=\|v\|_2\).  Conditional independence of the two projected observations and Jensen's inequality give, without restricting the donor event,
\[
 \mathbb E_P[d_n\mathbf1\{G_n\}]
 \le {K_0\sigma^2\ell_n\over n^2}
 (U_0/\sigma+\sqrt r+\sqrt{\ell_n})
 (V_0/\sigma+\sqrt r+\sqrt{\ell_n}).
\]
The spectrum and span conditions imply
\[
 a_n\ge {\sigma(U_0+V_0)\over\sqrt2C_0n},qquad
 b_n\ge {\sigma^2\over C_0n},qquad
 w_n\ge {\kappa(U_0+V_0+1)\over n},
\]
where \(\kappa=\min\{\sigma/(\sqrt2C_0),\sigma^2/C_0\}>0\).  Also \(U_0,V_0\le B\sqrt n\) and
\(U_0V_0/(U_0+V_0+1)\le B\sqrt n\).  Expanding the last product thus yields a constant \(K\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}{\mathbb E_P[d_n\mathbf1\{G_n\}]\over w_n}
 \le K\left({\ell_n\over\sqrt n}+{\ell_n^2\over n}\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves every assertion of the lemma without a target-loading lower bound.

Put \(h=\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), \(s=s_D(m)\), \(t=s/h\), and write \(Z=m+\xi\), where \(\xi=(\xi_p^{\top},\xi_q^{\top})^{\top}\sim N(0,I_{2r})\).  The exact bilinear expansion is
\[
 Z_p^{\top}DZ_q-m_p^{\top}Dm_q
 =\langle(Dm_q,D^{\top}m_p),\xi\rangle+\xi_p^{\top}D\xi_q,qquad
 |\xi_p^{\top}D\xi_q|\le {h\over2}\|\xi\|_2^2.
\]
The linear term is centered normal with variance \(s^2\), including the degenerate case \(s=0\).

We first record the radial bound implicit in the calibration.  For \(Y\sim\chi^2_d\), its moment-generating function and Chernoff optimization give
\[
 \Pr\{Y>d+2\sqrt{dx}+2x\}\le e^{-x}\qquad(x\ge0).
\]
With \(d=2r\) and \(x=\log(4(1+t)/\alpha)\), this and \(2\sqrt{dx}\le d+x\) imply
\[
 \rho_\alpha(t)^2\le C_{r,\alpha}\log(e+t).
\]
Hence the event
\[
 \|\xi\|_2\le\rho_\alpha(t),qquad
 |\langle(Dm_q,D^{\top}m_p),\xi\rangle|
 \le\zeta_\alpha(t)s
\]
has probability at least \(1-\beta_\alpha(t)-[\alpha-\beta_\alpha(t)]=1-\alpha\).  On this event the absolute bilinear error is at most
\[
 H(m):=h\left\{\zeta_\alpha(t)t+{C_{r,\alpha}\over2}\log(e+t)\right\}.
\]

It remains to show that the observable \(W\) dominates this quantity on the same event.  The map \(m\mapsto s_D(m)\) obeys
\[
 |s_D(Z)-s_D(m)|\le h\|Z-m\|_2,qquad |t_Z-t|\le\|\xi\|_2.
\]
If \(t>2t_Z\), then \(t/2<\sqrt{C_{r,\alpha}\log(e+t)}\).  For \(t\ge2\), \(\log(e+t)\le t\), and therefore \(t<4C_{r,\alpha}\); for \(t<2\) the same conclusion follows from the definition of \(A_{r,\alpha}\).  Thus in every case
\[
 t\le2t_Z+A_{r,\alpha},qquad
 |t-t_Z|\le R_0,qquad t_-\le t\le t_+.
\]
The function \(\zeta_\alpha\) is decreasing because \(\beta_\alpha\) is decreasing.  Consequently,
\[
 H(m)\le h\left\{\zeta_\alpha(t_-)t_+
 +{C_{r,\alpha}\over2}\log(e+t_+)\right\}=W.
\]
The stated interval therefore covers \(\sigma^2m_p^{\top}Dm_q\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).

For length, \(\zeta_\alpha(t)\le\Phi^{-1}(1-3\alpha/8)\).  Also \(R_0\le K_{r,\alpha}(1+\sqrt{t_Z})\), whence \(t_+\le K_{r,\alpha}(1+t_Z)\) and \(\log(e+t_+)\le K_{r,\alpha}(1+t_Z)\).  Therefore
\[
 W\le K_\alpha h(1+t_Z)=K_\alpha(h+s_D(Z)).
\]
Since \(\mathbb E_m s_D(Z)\le s_D(m)+h\mathbb E\|\xi\|_2\), fixed \(r\le r_0\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_m[2\sigma^2W]\le K_\alpha\sigma^2(s_D(m)+h),
\]
after absorbing the factor two into \(K_\alpha\).

Finally consider any deterministic triangular sequence with \(t=s_D(m)/h\to\infty\).  The inequality \(|t_Z-t|\le\|\xi\|_2=O_P(1)\) gives \(t_Z/t\to1\).  Hence \(R_0/t_Z\to0\), \(t_-/t\to1\), \(t_+/t\to1\), \(\zeta_\alpha(t_-)\to z_\alpha:=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\), and \(\log(e+t_+)/t\to0\), all in probability.  Thus
\[
 {W\over s_D(m)}\longrightarrow z_\alpha
\]
in probability, which is exactly the asserted length ratio.  This self-contained outer inversion is an explicit specialization of the first-order-degeneracy problem studied by Bei--Navjeevan~\cite{BeiNavjeevan2026}; no theorem from that paper is used as a premise here.

First, the fallback always covers the target.  Indeed, by the span and entry bounds,
\[
 |\theta_n|\le\|u\|_2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2
 \le (B\sqrt n){1\over cn}(B\sqrt n)=M_0.
\]
On \(G_n\), condition on \(X\).  The conditional-reduction lemma and the Gaussian-outer-inversion lemma show that the interval without the donor allowance covers \(\theta_{X,n}\) with conditional probability at least \(1-\alpha\).  If in addition \(|\theta_{X,n}-\theta_n|\le d_n\), enlarging both endpoints by \(d_n\) covers \(\theta_n\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P\{\theta_n\notin I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\}
 &\le P\{G_n,\ \theta_{X,n}\text{ is not covered centrally}\}
   +P\{G_n,\ |\theta_{X,n}-\theta_n|>d_n\}\\
 &\le\alpha+e^{-n/2}+3(e+n)^{-6}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), then the limit superior, proves the uniform coverage claim.  None of these inequalities divides by a loading or assumes it nonzero.  In particular the same argument applies at joint zero and along arbitrarily slow loading transitions.  For an explicit strictness witness, retain any admissible donor \(A\) and set \(u=v=0\).  This law belongs to \(\mathcal P_n\) and is covered by the displayed argument, but it violates every positive lower bound on either target loading.  The comparison with the loading-restricted Gaussian interval of Yan--Wainwright~\cite{YanWainwright2024} follows because the remaining strong-donor rank and span conditions are unchanged.

On \(G_n\), \(h_n\le2/(cn)\), and the span representations give
\[
 s_D(m_n)
 \le {h_n\over\sigma}(\|u\|_2+\|v\|_2)
 \le {2(\|u\|_2+\|v\|_2)\over c\sigma n}.
\]
The Gaussian-outer-inversion expectation bound, followed by the lower bound for \(w_n\) proved in \(\textnormal{lem:conditional-reduction}\), therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[2\sigma^2W_n\mathbf1\{G_n\}]
 \le K_\alpha {\|u\|_2+\|v\|_2+1\over n}
 \le K_\alpha w_n.
\]
The same lemma gives \(\mathbb E_P[2d_n\mathbf1\{G_n\}]=o(w_n)\) uniformly.  For sufficiently large \(n\), the event \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\sigma\sqrt n\) is contained in \(G_n\), so
\[
 P(G_n^c)\le e^{-n/2}.
\]
Since the off-gate length is \(2M_0\) and \(w_n\ge\sigma^2/(C_0n)\),
\[
 {2M_0P(G_n^c)\over w_n}
 \le {2M_0C_0n\over\sigma^2}e^{-n/2}=o(1)
\]
uniformly over the class.  Adding the three contributions proves the displayed uniform bound after enlarging \(K_\alpha\).  This also shows explicitly why the bounded spectral fallback does not alter the transition order.

Let \(U_0=\|u\|_2\), \(V_0=\|v\|_2\), and set \(a_{X,n}=\sigma^2s_D(m_n)\).  On \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le cn/4\), the same sandwich expansion used in \(\textnormal{lem:conditional-reduction}\), now retaining one unrestricted action, gives
\[
 \|(X_r^+-A^+)U\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \|V^{\top}(X_r^+-A^+)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le K{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\over n^2}.
\]
To see this directly, project \(X_r^+U-A^+U\) onto \(\operatorname{col}(V)\), where the preceding bound for \(T_X-S^{-1}\) applies with \(\gamma\le e_0\); its orthogonal projection is at most \(\lambda/(cn-e_0)\).  The transpose argument treats the other action.  Since
\[
 a_n\ge {\sigma(U_0+V_0)\over\sqrt2C_0n},
\]
the reverse triangle inequality yields, whenever \(a_n>0\),
\[
 \left|{a_{X,n}\over a_n}-1\right|
 \le K{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\over n}=o_P(1).
\]
The min--max perturbation inequality likewise gives
\[
 {\sigma^2\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_{mathrm F}\over b_n}\longrightarrow1
\]
in probability, uniformly over the strong-spectrum class.  As \(h_n\le\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_{mathrm F}\), the assumed \(b_n/a_n\to0\) implies
\[
 {s_D(m_n)\over h_n}={a_{X,n}\over\sigma^2h_n}\longrightarrow\infty
\]
in probability.

Conditional on \(X\), the last conclusion and the uniform deterministic tail argument in \(\textnormal{lem:gaussian-outer-inversion}\) imply
\[
 {\sigma^2W_n\over z_\alpha a_{X,n}}\longrightarrow1
\]
in probability on \(G_n\).  Moreover, the conditional-reduction expectation bound and \(w_n/a_n=1+b_n/a_n\to1\) give by Markov's inequality
\[
 {d_n\mathbf1\{G_n\}\over a_n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Finally \(P(G_n^c)\to0\).  On \(G_n\), the interval length equals \(2\sigma^2W_n+2d_n\); combining the last displays proves
\[
 {\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})}
 {2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n}\longrightarrow1
\]
in \(P_n\)-probability.  The argument uses only divergence of \(a_n/b_n\), so no deterministic divergence rate or hidden pretest is present.

When \(r=1\), write the retained singular triplet as \((\widehat u,\widehat s,\widehat v)\).  The center is exactly
\[
 \widehat\theta_n
 =\sigma^2Z_{p,n}D_nZ_{q,n}
 ={(R\widehat v)(\widehat u^{\top}C)\over\widehat s}
 =RX_r^+C,
\]
which is the rank-one four-block spectral plug-in center.  Its plug-in first-order standard error is
\[
 \widehat a_{X,n}:=\sigma^2s_{Z,n}
 =\sigma\left\{
 { (\widehat u^{\top}C)^2+(R\widehat v)^2\over\widehat s^2}
 \right\}^{1/2},
\]
the Gaussian variance formula used by Yan--Wainwright~\cite{YanWainwright2024}.  Under \(b_n/a_n\to0\), the proof of \(\textnormal{thm:oracle-length}\) gives \(a_{X,n}/a_n\to1\), while
\[
 |s_{Z,n}-s_D(m_n)|\le h_n\|\xi_n\|_2,qquad
 {\sigma^2h_n\over a_n}=O_P(b_n/a_n)=o_P(1).
\]
Thus \(\widehat a_{X,n}/a_n\to1\).  The explicit half-width satisfies \(\sigma^2W_n=z_\alpha\widehat a_{X,n}+o_P(a_n)\), and the donor allowance is \(o_P(a_n)\).  Hence both the center formula and the first-order half-width reduce to the cited regular rank-one construction up to the asserted \(o_P(a_n)\) remainder.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Starting move: for exact dyadic \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\), adaptively double \(q_n\) in \(\mathbb F_n^{\mathrm{dir}}\); use the coordinate boxes of radius \(2^{-p_n-1}\) about the dyadic arrays to propagate observation-encoding uncertainty through residual-certified enclosures of the retained singular values, invariant subspace, pseudoinverse, matrix products, and exact-real endpoints. Use a three-way accept--reject--uncertain spectral gate; the uncertain branch returns the outward hull of \([-M_0,M_0]\) and the certified on-gate enclosure. Enclose \(\Phi^{-1}(q)\) and \(F_{\chi^2_{2r}}^{-1}(q)\) in polynomial time by rational interval evaluation of the error and regularized incomplete-gamma functions followed by certified interval bisection or Newton steps until the enclosure of a quantile \(Q\) has width at most \(8\cdot2^{1-q_n}(1+|Q|)\). Record the propagated encoding radius as \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\), all SVD, gate, quantile, scalar-function, and endpoint-rounding radii as \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), and return \(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}}\) only with a containment certificate.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: With a \(q_n\)-bit normalized significand, adjacent representable numbers near a nonzero quantile are separated on the relative scale \(\eta_n|Q|\), so an absolute enclosure width \(2^{-q_n}\) is generally impossible even for a normal critical value between one and two. The corrected relative-plus-absolute tolerance is attainable by directed rounding and remains exponentially negligible under polynomial precision schedules. The deterministic certificate and the implementation OEQ must be re-solved after this construction correction is applied.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\delta\) and a sequence \(P_n=P_{A,u,v}\) satisfying the displayed interior conditions.  All objects below may depend on \(n\).  By \(\text{ass:exact-rank}\) and \(\text{ass:strong-spectrum}\), write the compact singular value decomposition as
\[
A=USV^{\mathsf T},\qquad D=S^{-1}.
\]
The matrix \(D\) is a positive diagonal \(r\)-by-\(r\) matrix.  By \(\text{ass:row-span}\) and \(\text{ass:column-span}\), the coordinates
\[
x=(uV)^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^r,qquad y=U^{\mathsf T}v\in\mathbb R^r
\]
satisfy \(u=x^{\mathsf T}V^{\mathsf T}\) and \(v=Uy\).  Hence the causal target specified in the statement, rather than a newly defined surrogate, obeys
\[
\theta_n(P_n)=uA^+v=x^{\mathsf T}Dy. \tag{1}
\]
Moreover, orthonormality of the columns of \(U,V\) and \(\text{def:transition-scale}\) give
\[
a_n=\sigma\bigl(\|Dx\|_2^2+\|Dy\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2},
\qquad
b_n=\sigma^2\|D\|_{\mathrm F},
\qquad w_n=a_n+b_n. \tag{2}
\]
In particular \(b_n>0\), because \(r\geq1\) and every diagonal entry of \(D\) is positive.

Set
\[
\tau=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}.
\]
The restriction \(0<\alpha<1/2\) implies \(0<\tau<1/2\).  We construct a finite collection of alternatives by keeping \(A\) fixed and changing only \((x,y)\).  First suppose \(a_n>0\).  For \(g(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}Dy\), one has
\[
\nabla g(x,y)=(Dy,Dx),
\qquad \|\nabla g(x,y)\|_2=a_n/\sigma.
\]
Let \((h_x,h_y)=\sigma\tau\nabla g/\|\nabla g\|_2\).  For each \(s\in\{-1,1\}\), define an alternative with coordinates \((x+s h_x,y+s h_y)\).  Its target displacement from (1) is
\[
\Delta_s
=s\{h_x^{\mathsf T}Dy+x^{\mathsf T}Dh_y\}+h_x^{\mathsf T}Dh_y
=s\tau a_n+h_x^{\mathsf T}Dh_y.
\]
Since \(\max\{|z+c|,|-z+c|\}\geq |z|\), these two alternatives satisfy
\[
\max_{s\in\{-1,1\}}|\Delta_s|\geq\tau a_n. \tag{3}
\]
If \(a_n=0\), inequality (3) is true with its right-hand side equal to zero and no first-order alternatives are needed.

For the second-order alternatives, choose \(j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\) such that \(D_{jj}=\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), put \(h_0=\sigma\tau/\sqrt2\), and, for \((s,t)\in\{-1,1\}^2\), use coordinates
\[
(x+s h_0 e_j,\ y+t h_0 e_j).
\]
Writing the corresponding target displacement as \(\Delta_{s,t}\), expansion of (1) yields
\[
\Delta_{s,t}
=s h_0(Dy)_j+t h_0(Dx)_j+st h_0^2D_{jj}.
\]
Taking the signed four-corner average cancels both linear terms:
\[
\frac14\sum_{s,t\in\{-1,1\}}st\Delta_{s,t}
=h_0^2D_{jj}
=\frac{\sigma^2\tau^2}{2}\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
The absolute value of an average with coefficients of absolute value one is at most the largest absolute summand.  Since \(r\leq r_0\) and \(\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\geq\|D\|_{\mathrm F}/\sqrt r\), (2) therefore implies
\[
\max_{s,t\in\{-1,1\}}|\Delta_{s,t}|
\geq\frac{\tau^2b_n}{2\sqrt{r_0}}. \tag{4}
\]

We next verify that all these alternatives are in the stated local model.  A coordinate perturbation \((h_x,h_y)\) is implemented by
\[
u'=u+h_x^{\mathsf T}V^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
v'=v+Uh_y.
\]
It preserves \(u'\in\operatorname{row}(A)\) and \(v'\in\operatorname{col}(A)\).  Every perturbation used above satisfies
\[
\|h_x\|_2^2+\|h_y\|_2^2=\sigma^2\tau^2. \tag{5}
\]
By the interior incoherence bound in the theorem and \(r\leq r_0\), for each coordinate \(k\),
\[
|(h_x^{\mathsf T}V^{\mathsf T})_k|
\leq\|h_x\|_2\|V_{k\boldsymbol\cdot}\|_2
\leq\sigma\tau\sqrt{\mu r_0/n},
\]
and the same bound holds for \(|(Uh_y)_k|\).  The right-hand side tends to zero.  Thus, for all sufficiently large \(n\), it is at most the fixed entry slack \(\delta\); together with \(\|u\|_\infty,\|v\|_\infty\leq B-\delta\), this proves \(\|u'\|_\infty,\|v'\|_\infty\leq B\).  The matrix \(A\), and hence its rank, singular values, singular spaces, incoherence, and entry bound, is unchanged.  Keeping the Gaussian covariance fixed preserves \(\text{ass:gaussian-blocks}\).  Consequently every constructed law is in \(\mathcal P_n\) by \(\text{def:model-class}\).

Orthonormality and (5) show
\[
\|u-u'\|_2^2+\|v-v'\|_2^2
=\|h_x\|_2^2+\|h_y\|_2^2
=\sigma^2\tau^2.
\]
Since \(A\) is unchanged, \(\text{def:local-neighborhood}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_n,Q)=\tau^2/2<1
\tag{6}
\]
for each constructed alternative \(Q\).  Hence all of them belong to \(\mathcal N_n(P_n)\).

For completeness, we derive directly the probability comparison needed below from \(\text{ass:gaussian-blocks}\), without invoking an undeclared testing result.  The joint data densities \(p,q\) under \(P_n,Q\) have common covariance \(\sigma^2I\), and their mean vectors are separated by Euclidean norm \(\sigma\tau\).  Completing the square in their Gaussian densities gives
\[
\int\sqrt{pq}=\exp(-\tau^2/8).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{TV}(P_n,Q)
&=\frac12\int|p-q|\\
&\leq\frac12
 \left\{\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \left\{\int(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
&=\sqrt{1-\left(\int\sqrt{pq}\right)^2}
=\sqrt{1-e^{-\tau^2/4}}
\leq\tau/2,
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(1-e^{-z}\leq z\) for \(z\geq0\).

Now define the uniform coverage level
\[
\gamma_n=\inf_{H\in\mathcal P_n}H\{\theta_n(H)\in J_n\},
\qquad
\varepsilon_n=(1-\alpha-\gamma_n)_+.
\]
The assumed uniform honesty of \(J_n\) implies \(\varepsilon_n\to0\).  Thus, for every \(H\in\mathcal P_n\),
\[
H\{\theta_n(H)\in J_n\}\geq1-\alpha-\varepsilon_n. \tag{8}
\]
For any one of the constructed alternatives \(Q\), (7), (8), and the union bound under \(P_n\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_n\{\theta_n(P_n)\in J_n,\ \theta_n(Q)\in J_n\}
&\geq P_n\{\theta_n(P_n)\in J_n\}
   +P_n\{\theta_n(Q)\in J_n\}-1\\
&\geq1-2\alpha-2\varepsilon_n-\operatorname{TV}(P_n,Q)\\
&\geq1-2\alpha-2\varepsilon_n-\tau/2. 
\end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
On the event in (9), the interval \(J_n\) contains both target values, so its length is at least \(|\theta_n(Q)-\theta_n(P_n)|\).

Choose from the finite collection an alternative \(Q_n^\star\) with largest absolute target displacement.  Equations (3) and (4) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\theta_n(Q_n^\star)-\theta_n(P_n)|
&\geq\max\left\{\tau a_n,\frac{\tau^2b_n}{2\sqrt{r_0}}\right\}\\
&\geq\frac{\tau^2}{4\sqrt{r_0}}(a_n+b_n)
=\frac{\tau^2}{4\sqrt{r_0}}w_n. 
\end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
The second inequality follows from \(\max\{z_1,z_2\}\geq(z_1+z_2)/2\) and \(\tau^2/(2\sqrt{r_0})\leq\tau\).  Combining (9)--(10), with the conclusion immediate if the expected length is infinite, yields
\[
\frac{\mathbb E_{P_n}[\operatorname{length}(J_n)]}{w_n(P_n)}
\geq
\frac{\tau^2}{4\sqrt{r_0}}
\left(1-2\alpha-2\varepsilon_n-\frac\tau2\right).
\tag{11}
\]
Finally \(P_n\in\mathcal N_n(P_n)\) because its Kullback--Leibler divergence from itself is zero.  Therefore the left-hand side of (11) is bounded above by the supremum appearing in the theorem.  Taking lower limits and substituting \(\tau=(1-2\alpha)/2\) proves the claim with the explicit positive choice
\[
k_\alpha
=\frac{\tau^2}{4\sqrt{r_0}}
  \left(1-2\alpha-\frac\tau2\right)
=\frac{3\tau^2(1-2\alpha)}{16\sqrt{r_0}}>0.
\]
